### Differentiation of Self
A concept from Bowen theory referring to the degree to which a person has a solid, defined sense of self. In the transcript, Kerr describes two ways it can be raised: through "an organized effort in their own family" or through "an unusual life experience." The interviewee describes achieving "a notch of differentiation" as a result of her cancer diagnosis and subsequent self-examination, manifesting as reduced reactivity and greater ability to see her own role in relationship patterns.

### Pseudo Self
A false or constructed self that a person presents or operates from, as distinct from a more genuine, solid self. The interviewee describes experiencing "a literal separation process in me from this person I had been building, you know, constructing," and recognizes that the pseudo self had effectively been "living my life in my place." It is associated with borrowed beliefs and identity rather than one's own deeply held convictions.

### Solid Self
The genuine, stable core of a person's identity, contrasted with the pseudo self. In the transcript it is described in terms of having firm convictions — referencing Bowen's challenge of asking people "what principles and beliefs would you be willing to die for?" — and is associated with functioning that does not depend on borrowing identity from relationships or external sources.

### Nodal Events
Significant life events that cluster together and place stress on an individual's functioning. The interviewee lists several occurring around 2015 — her mother's death, loss of her dog, her mother-in-law's dementia and accusations, and her husband's retirement — describing them not as individually decisive but collectively as things that "unmasked the story" and overwhelmed her limited sense of self.

### Pursuer-Distancer Pattern
A relational dynamic in which one partner characteristically pursues emotional engagement while the other distances or withdraws. The interviewee identifies herself as "a pursuer" and her husband as someone whose "tendency to close up and distance himself has been his mode of survival all of his life," describing the pattern as "disastrous for many years."

### Loss of Self
A process by which a person's genuine identity erodes over time, often within a highly fused relationship or life context. The interviewee describes a "slow loss of self" beginning with her marriage in 1991, leaving her with "a very small me" by the time the nodal events of 2015 occurred, rendering her unable to navigate those stressors effectively.

### Open Relationship
A concept attributed to Murray Bowen in the transcript, described as a relationship in which "each person can talk about their innermost feelings and thoughts to this other person without the fear of the other person being reactive and vice versa." Kerr suggests the interviewee's relationship with God approximates this quality.

### Fusion
A state of emotional togetherness or enmeshment in a relationship that compromises individual selfhood. The interviewee describes entering "a very fusional relationship" with her husband, a new country, and a new family, which she identifies as a key context for her slow loss of self.

### Emotional Cutoff
Referenced in the Q&A as a pattern in which people, rather than building self within their existing relationships and life, exit one pseudo self for another — described as exchanging "one suit of self for an alternative one" — mistaking this substitution for genuine growth of self.

### Function of Belief
A framing introduced by Kerr to describe how religious or spiritual belief operates practically in a person's life regardless of whether it can be empirically verified. Kerr states that "the belief supports it being functional," and uses this concept to explain how Bowen incorporated supernatural phenomena into his theory — not by proving or disproving them, but by recognizing their measurable effect on human functioning.
